title: Threads and CMake
summary: Link the platform thread library and reason about shared state.

scenario.briefing: A worker binary uses std::thread but the CMake target does not link the platform thread library, so the build fails on Linux. Repair the target, then reason about a shared counter.

objectives.description: Find and link the platform thread library in CMake.
Choose synchronization for a shared counter.
Explain joins, data races, and CMake targets accurately.

hints: CMake has a package for platform threads.
Call find_package(Threads REQUIRED) before the target.

misconceptions.description: Compiling without linking the thread library.
misconceptions.feedback: std::thread needs the platform thread library. Find the Threads package and link Threads::Threads to the target.

misconceptions.description: Using volatile as a synchronization primitive.
misconceptions.feedback: volatile controls compiler optimizations, not atomicity or ordering. Use a mutex or std::atomic.

misconceptions.description: Believing a detached thread finishes before main exits.
misconceptions.feedback: A detached thread runs independently. If main exits first, the process can terminate while the thread is still using its data.

sections.title: Threads need a join or a plan
sections.body: std::thread starts a new thread of execution. A joinable thread must be joined or detached before it is destroyed, or the program terminates. Join when the result matters; detach only when the work truly outlives the current scope and owns everything it touches.

sections.title: Shared writes need synchronization
sections.body: Two threads incrementing the same int without synchronization create a data race, which is undefined behavior. A mutex protects a critical section, and std::atomic provides indivisible operations for simple shared values. volatile is not a synchronization tool in C++.

sections.title: CMake carries platform requirements
sections.body: Threads are part of the platform toolchain, so CMake needs find_package(Threads REQUIRED) and target_link_libraries(... Threads::Threads). The same target model links sockets or other system libraries. Keep the requirements on the target that uses them.

steps.prompt: Edit CMakeLists.txt. Require the platform Threads package and link Threads::Threads to campus_worker.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(campus_worker CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

add_executable(campus_worker main.cpp)

steps.title: Protect the shared counter
steps.prompt: Two threads increment the same int. Which change removes the data race?

options.label: Guard the increment with std::mutex or use std::atomic<int>.
Detach both threads and let main exit.

quiz.explanation: A mutex makes the read-modify-write atomic as a critical section. std::atomic provides an atomic increment directly. volatile and sleeps do not provide synchronization.

hints: The race is on a read-modify-write sequence.
Sleeping changes timing but not atomicity.
Use a mutex or an atomic type.
Choose the mutex or atomic option.

steps.title: Joins, races, and targets

statements.label: A joinable thread must be joined or detached before it is destroyed.
A mutex can protect a read-modify-write sequence from a data race.
A detached thread always finishes before main exits.
CMake can attach link requirements to a specific target.

steps.explanation: Thread lifetime needs an explicit decision. A mutex or atomic protects shared writes, and CMake keeps link requirements on the target that needs them.
hints: Detached work is not awaited by main.
CMake target properties do not leak to unrelated targets.
